title: A tidal disruption event in a quasar at redshift 7.19
comment: 18 pages, 8 (+2) figures, 1 table. Submitted to OJA. Comments are welcome!
summary: We report a long-lived nuclear transient in GNz7q, a red quasar at $z=7.19$ powered by a $\sim3\times10^{7}\,M_\odot$ black hole and hosted by a compact, dusty starburst galaxy. The transient was identified in more than two decades of imaging with HST, Spitzer, and JWST. After a rapid rise, the source faded smoothly by $Δm\simeq1.1$ mag in the rest-frame ultraviolet over $\sim2$ rest-frame yr, with coherent, wavelength-dependent evolution across 1--5 $μ$m that places GNz7q above the 99.9th percentile of the SDSS quasar variability distribution and is absent at $z\gtrsim5$. The duration and energetics disfavor superluminous supernovae, and stochastic quasar variability reproduces the multi-band evolution with a probability of $\lesssim10^{-5}$. A panchromatic model combining a thermal continuum with a $t^{-5/3}$ decline reproduces the light curves, yielding a peak bolometric luminosity of $\simeq3\times10^{45}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and a radiated energy of $\simeq1.5\times10^{53}$ erg, which imply the tidal disruption of a star of a few solar masses and place the event among the most energetic tidal disruption events (TDEs) known. A redshifted, extremely broad Balmer-line component in independent JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy is consistent with a transient, non-virialized broad-line region. JWST/MIRI photometry further reveals delayed mid-infrared emission from $\simeq1500$ K dust at a sub-parsec radius, consistent with a dust echo of the flare. The relatively low black-hole mass and dense star-forming nucleus of GNz7q are conditions under which TDEs are expected to be most efficient. These observations provide a time-domain view of episodic black-hole fueling and its dusty nuclear environment 700 million years after the Big Bang. Wide-field surveys with Roman and Euclid in the near-infrared, complemented by LSST at lower redshifts, may uncover such transients in large numbers.

AI.tldr: 本文报告了在红移z=7.19的高红移类星体GNz7q中发现的一个长寿命核瞬变事件，其特征与潮汐撕裂事件（TDE）高度一致，是目前已知最遥远、最明亮的TDE之一，揭示了早期宇宙中超大质量黑洞吸积的时域特征及周围尘埃环境。
AI.motivation: 在高红移（z>5）宇宙中探测和确认潮汐撕裂事件（TDE）极为罕见，而理解早期黑洞如何通过 episodic 过程（如TDE）被喂食，对研究黑洞-星系共同演化至关重要；本文旨在利用多代空间望远镜长期监测数据，识别并证认一个发生在宇宙年龄仅约7亿年的极端TDE候选体。
AI.method: 综合分析哈勃（HST）、斯皮策（Spitzer）和韦布（JWST）长达二十余年的多波段成像数据，结合JWST/NIRSpec光谱和MIRI中红外测光，开展光变建模（含t^{-5/3}衰减+热连续谱）、统计检验（排除超亮超新星与随机类星体变源）、光谱特征分析（红移宽巴尔末线）及尘埃回波建模。
AI.result: 确认GNz7q中存在一例持续约2年静止帧、紫外波段变幅达1.1等、总辐射能量~1.5×10^53 erg、峰值光度~3×10^45 erg/s的核瞬变；其光变、光谱（非维里化宽线）、中红外延迟辐射（~1500 K尘埃回波）均支持一颗数倍太阳质量恒星被~3×10^7 M⊙黑洞潮汐撕裂；该事件位于SDSS类星体变异性分布的99.9%以上分位。
AI.conclusion: GNz7q中的瞬变是迄今最遥远、最有力的高红移TDE证据，表明在致密星暴星系核中，低质量黑洞可高效产生TDE；这为早期宇宙黑洞间歇性吸积提供了直接时域观测支持，并预示未来Roman、Euclid与LSST联合巡天有望大规模发现此类事件。
